notes: No product called "SCX-25" exists in Biamp's lineup; the request has been fulfilled against the actual Biamp product "Devio SCR-25" (a desktop conferencing hub), which is the closest real match — Biamp's SCX series (SCX-400/SCX-800) are rack-style conference room hubs with a completely different, network/AVB-based I/O set, so SCX-25 is not simply a naming variant of either family. All ports below are sourced from Biamp's official SCR-25 data sheet (back-panel diagram, front-panel diagram, and Architects & Engineers spec section), DEVDS-506-2105-EN-R1. HDMI Input is HDCP 1.4, supports up to 3840x2160@30Hz (2160p only on Output Port 1); no HDMI version (1.4/2.0/2.1) is explicitly stated in the datasheet, so grade is omitted for HDMI ports rather than guessed. USB ports are stated as USB 3.0 Type-A (front x2, rear x1) and USB Type-B (front, host-facing upstream port, functions as USB Class 1 Audio device) — USB version for the Type-B port is not explicitly stated, so no grade was assigned to it; the Type-A ports are graded usb-5g (USB 3.0/3.1 Gen1 = 5Gbps) per the datasheet's explicit "USB 3.0" callout. RJ-45 network port has no stated Ethernet speed in the datasheet (only "RJ-45 with Ethernet cable, Cat 5e and above"), so grade is omitted rather than assumed. The second RJ-45 port is a proprietary Beamtracking microphone input (RJ-45 connector per A&E spec) — not a network/data Ethernet port — so it is modeled as input-only with no eth grade. Power input is a 4-pin locking DC connector (24V DC, 2.5A/60W external supply); no connector ID in the allowed list exactly matches Biamp's proprietary 4-pin locking barrel-style DC connector, so xlr4-dc was chosen as the closest analog (4-pin DC power connector) — actual physical connector is a proprietary locking DC barrel plug, not true XLR. Headset jack is a 4P4C (RJ9-style) telephony connector; no exact match exists in the allowed connector list, so it was omitted from ports rather than mis-tagged (closest would be rj45 but that is inaccurate enough to mislead on cabling — noting here per instructions). Speaker terminal block output (+/-) for the built-in 20W amplifier is modeled as euroblock (closest match to a captive screw-terminal block).
